title: Corrected boundary-confirmation plan of survey
mainQuestion: What should a learner remember about Corrected boundary-confirmation plan of survey?
studySummary: Subject to subsection (3), the Registrar General may, on receiving satisfactory evidence, order that a corrected plan of survey be made in order to correct any inconsistency, error or omission in a plan of survey that has been filed under subsection 15(1). The Registrar General may give such notice to interested parties as the Registrar General considers appropriate before making an order under subsection (1) or may make the order without giving notice. A correction under this section shall not affect the location of a boundary that has been confirmed and certified under this Act. The Registrar General shall cause a corrected plan of survey made under subsection (1) to be filed in accordance with the regulations and with the Registry Act or the Land Titles Act, as the case may be. Subsection 15(2) applies with the necessary modifications to a corrected plan of survey filed under subsection (4). When a corrected plan of survey is filed under subsection (4), the Registrar General shall cause a notation to be made on the plan of survey filed under subsection 15(1) to which the corrected plan relates, to the effect that it is superseded by the corrected plan.

title: Director of Surveys designation and coordinate monument duties
mainQuestion: What should a learner remember about Director of Surveys designation and coordinate monument duties?
studySummary: Service New Brunswick shall designate a surveyor as Director of Surveys. Service New Brunswick may designate one or more surveyors to perform any of the duties or exercise any of the powers of the Director of Surveys that are specified in the designation. Only a surveyor who is an employee of Service New Brunswick or an employee under the Civil Service Act is eligible to be designated under subsection (1.1). For the purposes of the coordinate survey system, the Director of Surveys shall establish and maintain coordinate monuments each being a brass, bronze or aluminum cap or plate suitably inscribed and (a) imbedded in a reinforced concrete post set in a concrete base, or (b) placed as prescribed by the regulations.
